title: The Tortoise and the Two Cranes
summary: A talkative tortoise is carried by two friends to a new lake. All he has to do is stay silent along the way.
moral: Listen to the advice of friends, hold back from showing off, and do not speak when there is no need.
pages: A long dry season dried up the pond where the tortoise lived. The grass turned yellow and the ground cracked. The tortoise sat wearily at the edge of the pond. 'Where shall I go?' it groaned.
Two cranes, the tortoise's friends, came over. 'Do not be sad, friend,' they said. 'We know a big lake with clear water, but it is very far away.' The tortoise's eyes sparkled.
'Bite this stick tightly, and we will carry you flying,' said the two cranes. 'But remember: whatever happens, do not open your mouth.' The tortoise agreed.
So they flew high. The tortoise gripped the stick firmly while looking at the beautiful scenery below: villages, rice fields, and winding rivers.
The people in the village looked up and cried, 'Look! A tortoise can fly! Surely he thought of it himself!' The tortoise felt proud and longed to say, 'It was my idea!' His face looked restless.
The tortoise could hold back no longer. He opened his mouth to answer, and at once the stick slipped. The tortoise fell sliding down, while the two cranes cried, 'We warned you!'

Luckily the tortoise fell onto a pile of soft straw, so he was not badly hurt, only very embarrassed. The two cranes helped him until they reached the lake. The tortoise promised to always listen to his friends' advice. The end.
